skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

25.   (lib.rs:243) carries **no** `#[verus_spec]` — `bump_allocator` is not verified, so the

48. I tried, per function. Exact errors from every approach:
49. 
50. #### Attempt A — `ensure_pte` (`identity_map.rs:627`), admit removed
51. Minimal body (no admit). Verus output:
52. ```
53. error: postcondition not satisfied
54.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:618:13
55.     |
56. 618 |             Ok(_) => identity_map_view().mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr as int)),
57.     |             ^^^^^ failed this postcondition
58. ...
59. 639 |         return Ok(());
60. 
61. error: precondition not satisfied
62.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:631:40
63.     |
64. 631 |     let pte: PageTableEntry = unsafe { pt.read(pte_idx) }.ok_or_else(|| {
65.     |                                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
66.    ::: src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs:205:13   (requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)
67. ```
68. - **L618** is the headline blocker. `identity_map_view()` is `uninterp spec fn ... ->
69.   IdentityMapView` (spec.rs:36) — a **parameter-free, hence constant** function, so
70.   `identity_map_view().mapped` is a fixed unknown `Set`. The `Ok` arm must prove the page is
71.   in it and the `Err` arm must prove it is *not* — but the return path is unrelated to that
72.   fixed set. The existing lemmas only act on an arbitrary `v: IdentityMapView`; firing them
73.   needs the fact `identity_map_view() == old.spec_install_page(spec_page_base(phys_addr))`,
74.   which is exactly the **ghost-token attachment** the spec/TCB notes defer. It does not exist
75.   in the codebase, and asserting it without proof is an `assume` in disguise (forbidden).
76.   Confirming there is no spec hook: `PageTableEntry::is_present` (pte.rs:415) and
77.   `PageTableEntry::new` (pte.rs:317) have **no `#[verus_spec]`** — nothing ties the exec
78.   `pt.write(...)` to `identity_map_view().mapped`.
79. 
80. #### Attempt B — discharge the `read` precondition via the type invariant
81. Added `proof! { use_type_invariant(pte_idx); }`:
82. ```
83. error: Verus Internal Error: missing type invariant function
84.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:632:33
85. ```
86. - `TableIndex`'s `#[verifier::type_invariant] inv(&self) -> bool { self@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH }`
87.   lives in the **arch** crate (table.spec.rs:24); `use_type_invariant` on it from the
88.   **kernel** crate triggers a Verus internal error (cross-crate type invariants are not
89.   exported). This is a genuine Verus limitation (item 7). The only in-rules alternative —
90.   adding `requires pte_idx@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` to `ensure_pte` — is a **spec weakening**
91.   (adds a `requires`), which is forbidden.
92. 
93. #### Attempt C — `ensure_pt` (`identity_map.rs:533`), admit removed
94. ```
95. error: precondition not satisfied
96.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:534:44
97. 534 |     let pde: PageDirectoryEntry = unsafe { pd.read(pde_idx) }.ok_or_else(|| {
98.    ::: src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs:205:13   (requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)
99. 
100. error: precondition not satisfied
101.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:549:9
102. 549 | /         PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR
103. 550 | |             .alloc_as::<[PteWord; PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH]>()
104.     | |_______________________________________________________^   (requires bump_view(self).inv())
105. ```
106. - `pd.read` precondition: same cross-crate type-invariant wall as Attempt B.
107. - `alloc_as` requires `bump_view(self).inv()` (lib.rs:350) for the module-static
108.   `PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR`. There is no spec-readable invariant for that static — it would
109.   need a ghost attachment to the singleton, same deferral.
110. - The `Ok` alignment postcondition is **partly** provable (present-PDE path:
111.   `frame_address` ensures `% FRAME_SIZE == 0`, and `FRAME_SIZE == PAGE_SIZE ==
112.   spec_page_size()`), but the fresh-alloc path (`slot.as_ptr() as usize`) is not: the
113.   `<[T]>::as_ptr` `assume_specification` has an empty contract and is not linked to the
114.   allocator's `slot_ref_addr` alignment. Tightening `as_ptr` universally is unsound (a
115.   slice ptr is not generally page-aligned). Because a removed `admit()` must discharge the
116.   *whole* body, the unprovable preconditions above fail regardless.
117. 
118. #### Attempt D — `identity_map_page` (`identity_map.rs:718`), admit removed
119. ```
120. error: postcondition not satisfied
121.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:706:13
122. 706 |             Ok(_) => identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@),
123.     |             ^^^^^ failed this postcondition          (3 instances: pre-init no-op arm,
124.                                                             ensure_pt? arm, ensure_pte tail)
125. ```
126. - `accessible(p) := !initialized || mapped.contains(p)` over the same opaque constant view.
127.   No spec link from the exec `pd_paddr == 0` test to `identity_map_view().initialized`, nor
128.   from `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte` to `mapped`. Same ghost-token deferral.
129.

131. Removed `#[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]` above `error!("ensure_pt(): {reason}")`:
132. ```
133. error: Unsupported constant type
134.    --> src/kernel/src/macros.rs:188:12
135.     = note: this error originates in the macro `write` ... expansion of the macro `error`
136. error: could not compile `kernel` (bin "kernel") ... (verus did not run)
137. ```
138. - `error!` is **not** Verus-compilable; the cfg-gate is mandatory and skill-sanctioned.
139.   Reverted.
140. 
141. ### What unblocking requires (for the driver)
142. 
143. All four primary failures reduce to one missing piece: `identity_map_view()` must stop being
144. an opaque parameter-free constant and become a concrete function of **spec-readable global
145. state** that the exec writes update. Building that within this task is not possible because:
146. 1. It needs a spec-readable value of the `KERNEL_PD_PADDR` atomic. `KERNEL_PD_PADDR:
147.    AtomicUsize` is a plain `core` atomic with no Verus ghost/permission. Replacing it with a
148.    verified atomic changes the `load`/`store` sites in **`init`** and **`sync_kernel_pdes`**,
149.    which are **out of scope** ("do not touch unlisted functions").
150. 2. It needs `arch::…::Table::write` to expose an `old@ -> @` slot-update postcondition;
151.    `tcb-allowed.md` records that this is **deliberately omitted** (a contents postcondition on
152.    that `external_body` write was shown unsound), and `table.rs` is out of scope.
153. 3. Threading a `tracked` token through `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`/`identity_map_page` would
154.    change their signatures, breaking out-of-scope callers (`init`, `memcpy`, `memset`,
155.    `ensure_identity_mapped_range`).
156. 
157. Every sibling module (`mm/phys/*`) is in the identical deferred state (still carries exec
158. `admit()`s for the same opaque-view reason), so this is a cross-module framework decision,
159. not a local proof gap. Guidance needed: either (i) authorize the verified-atomic +
160. `Table::write` transition infrastructure (which spans out-of-scope modules/functions), or
161. (ii) accept these three exec obligations as proving-phase-deferred (tracked in
162. `verification-todo.md`) until that infrastructure lands. No spec was weakened and no
163. `assume`/`external_body`/`admit`-disguise was introduced to paper over the gap.
164.

 ### What unblocking requires (for the driver)
 
 All four primary failures reduce to one missing piece: `identity_map_view()` must stop being
 an opaque parameter-free constant and become a concrete function of **spec-readable global
 state** that the exec writes update. Building that within this task is not possible because:
 1. It needs a spec-readable value of the `KERNEL_PD_PADDR` atomic. `KERNEL_PD_PADDR:
    AtomicUsize` is a plain `core` atomic with no Verus ghost/permission. Replacing it with a
    verified atomic changes the `load`/`store` sites in **`init`** and **`sync_kernel_pdes`**,
    which are **out of scope** ("do not touch unlisted functions").
 2. It needs `arch::…::Table::write` to expose an `old@ -> @` slot-update postcondition;
    `tcb-allowed.md` records that this is **deliberately omitted** (a contents postcondition on
    that `external_body` write was shown unsound), and `table.rs` is out of scope.
 3. Threading a `tracked` token through `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`/`identity_map_page` would
    change their signatures, breaking out-of-scope callers (`init`, `memcpy`, `memset`,
    `ensure_identity_mapped_range`).
 
 Every sibling module (`mm/phys/*`) is in the identical deferred state (still carries exec
 `admit()`s for the same opaque-view reason), so this is a cross-module framework decision,
 not a local proof gap. Guidance needed: either (i) authorize the verified-atomic +
 `Table::write` transition infrastructure (which spans out-of-scope modules/functions), or
 (ii) accept these three exec obligations as proving-phase-deferred (tracked in
 `verification-todo.md`) until that infrastructure lands. No spec was weakened and no
 `assume`/`external_body`/`admit`-disguise was introduced to paper over the gap.
